summary: This lane's diff (0 migrations, 19 files, runtime/db/web CI+test infrastructure only) is unusually high quality against the house standards: every commit is a genuine TDD vertical slice (mixed test+implementation, never a battery of red tests before code), every ticket's report documents a public-seam test, a non-vacuity control, and — for #1044/#1128/#1129/#1141 — an actual red/green/restore cycle against the real committed cell, which I independently re-ran and confirmed. Docs (module READMEs, CONTEXT.md house term/_Avoid_ shape) are updated in the same commits as the code they describe and are accurate against what is on disk. The one real standards gap is #1131's vacuity control, which was performed against a hand-reconstructed equivalent of the new cell rather than the committed cell itself inside its real file — a real, but self-disclosed and substantially mitigated, deviation from WORK-ORDER.md's rule 4 vacuity-control requirement. One minor Duplicated Code smell (judgement call, matches a pre-existing pattern in the same file) is also noted.

findings.title: Vacuity control for #1131's new CLI-exit-code cell was performed on a hand-reconstructed equivalent, not on the committed cell inside two-build-cutover-e2e.mjs
findings.evidence: reports/waveS-lane06-ticket1131.md, 'Red/green, proven WITHOUT running the full two-build drill' and 'Anything unverified': the report states plainly that packages/runtime/tests/two-build-cutover-e2e.mjs 'was not executed end to end in this session.' In its place the implementer manually built a disposable WDK World clone and drove scripts/rollback-preflight.mjs's CLI directly (the same preflight()/frontierRuleViolations() call chain the new cell's runPreflightCli helper spawns), then broke and restored packages/runtime/lib/rollback-preflight.mjs's FRONTIER_RULES table by hand to see red/green. WORK-ORDER.md's addendum for wave 3, rule 4's last bullet, is explicit: 'A ticket whose whole deliverable is a test or a lint still needs the vacuity control: show the new cell FAILING against a deliberately broken subject once, then restore the subject byte for byte.' The literal committed cell (the new block at packages/runtime/tests/two-build-cutover-e2e.mjs:990-1057) was never itself run, red or green, inside its real execution context (main()'s real w1/w2/frontierVersion/preRuleBodies/requiredBodies values from a real two-build cycle) in this session.
findings.required_fix: Either the integrator or CI's own db-live-gates run should be treated as this cell's FIRST real execution (as the report itself flags), or a follow-up should run packages/runtime/tests/two-build-cutover-e2e.mjs end-to-end once before merge to close the gap. Mitigating: I independently re-verified the new block's variable scoping (preRuleBodies, requiredBodies, w1, w2, query, frontierVersion are all defined earlier in the same function) and re-ran eslint/tsc clean on the file, which substantially reduces (but does not eliminate) the risk of a scope or naming mistake the report's own 'Anything unverified' section names as the residual risk.

findings.title: Three near-identical $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY-writing shell blocks in .github/actions/frontier-leg/action.yml
findings.evidence: .github/actions/frontier-leg/action.yml gains the same 7-line `{ echo ...; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` Markdown-table block three times (the slice-list step, the cross-slice contract-roster step, the isolated-drill step), differing only in the header text and in FLOOR/SKIPMAX vs DFLOOR/DSKIPMAX variable names. A Fowler 'Duplicated Code' smell by the letter.
findings.required_fix: Judgement call, not a blocker: the file's existing FLOOR/SKIPMAX check blocks were already duplicated three times before this ticket (one per step), so this change follows the file's own established convention rather than introducing a new one. Fix, if a future touch to this file is worth it, would be a small shared shell function (or a `scripts/ci/write-step-summary.sh` sourced by each step) taking the header and the six values as arguments — GitHub composite-action steps cannot share in-process state, so the extraction is a script-file extraction, not a plain function-in-scope one.
